topics.topic: Authoritative Registry-address lifecycle and configuration ownership
questions: Which Registry-address lifecycle is authoritative, and must the State 0 passage be replaced to agree with A30?
Must State 0 be changed so that the Registry address is a required start-up setting read through RuntimeSettings, rather than an exception read by the gateway at each call?
Which text governs the Registry address: per-call environment reading with absence tolerated at start-up, or one start-up read into `RuntimeSettings` with absence fatal?

quotes:
The service is configured only by environment variables, which it validates when it starts
(except the Registry address, which the Registry gateway reads at each call
and whose absence fails only Registry calls, State 2 A30), and answers only on the trusted hosts it is
configured with; wildcard hosts and origins are refused.

The Registry URL is read only through `runtime_settings` (owner decision
2026-11-09, SPEC_STANDARD 6.11: a second reader of the environment is a
defect). `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` is a required variable of the start-up table that
R0-10's check covers, read into the `registry_base_url` field of
`RuntimeSettings`: a missing or empty value stops the start, and the Registry
gateway takes the value from the settings `load_runtime_settings` returns,
never from the environment.
judgement.divergence: With REGISTRY_BASE_URL absent, State 0 permits start-up and defers failure until a Registry call, while A30 stops start-up; the deployment operator observes the difference.
judgement.why: State 0 retains the superseded per-call Registry-address lifecycle while A30 makes the address a required start-up setting.

topics.topic: Precedence among Registry failure-translation conditions

quotes:
Every failed Registry call is answered with exactly one kind of the table and never with a

PLAT-REG-005: a focused test of the three gateway operations against a stubbed Registry, one case per member of `RegistryFailureKind` the gateway raises: a request timeout gives `timeout`; a connection failure and an unusable Registry URL give `transport_error`; an HTTP 404 gives `not_found`; any other non-success status gives `http_error`; an undecodable or invalid body gives `schema_mismatch`; a decoded answer for another project gives `identity_mismatch`. topics.topic: Normalization and rejection rules for source-supplied datetimes
questions: For every source-supplied datetime, are naive inputs rejected or interpreted as UTC, and are offset-aware inputs converted to UTC before their offset is removed?
Are offset-naive source datetimes rejected, interpreted as UTC, or interpreted using some other declared offset before being stored as offset-naive UTC?

quotes: import_snapshot: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it creates and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself. A supplied `approved_at` or `published_at` that carries a UTC offset MUST be converted to UTC, keeping its instant, before the publication reaches build_approved_estimate_snapshot, so it is stored offset-naive; a supplied offset-naive value is taken as UTC.

create_expense_from_recognition: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it creates and every current-time comparison it makes; the publication's `confirmed_at` is copied as confirmed, never replaced by it; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself. A supplied `confirmed_at` that carries a UTC offset MUST be converted to UTC, keeping its instant, before it is stored offset-naive; a supplied offset-naive value is taken as UTC.

publish_progress_photo: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself. A supplied `photo_date` that carries a UTC offset MUST be converted to UTC, keeping its instant, before it is stored offset-naive; a supplied offset-naive value is taken as UTC.
judgement.why: The State 7 notes require offset-aware values to be converted to UTC with the instant preserved and treat offset-naive supplied values as UTC.

What exact base-URL normalization and path-joining rule must generated code use, including trailing slashes and an existing base path?

quotes: _registry_url: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST join only the supplied relative path to the Registry deployment URL, which is the registry_base_url field of the RuntimeSettings that the imported load_runtime_settings returns when this function calls it, and MUST preserve that URL's own path prefix so a Registry deployed under a prefix keeps it on every request; it MUST NOT read the process environment itself. A missing or empty URL never reaches this function, because load_runtime_settings refuses the service start for it, and this function MUST NOT catch, translate or repair a refusal of load_runtime_settings. Each of the following MUST raise RegistryBoundaryError carrying the transport_error member of = models.RegistryFailureKind, never a raw ValueError or other untyped error, and never a repaired URL: the URL is not a usable http or https base URL; it carries userinfo credentials, which are rejected rather than stripped, retained, or forwarded; the supplied path is absolute or protocol-relative, which MUST NOT be allowed to replace the host or scheme.

list_active_projects: [PROVENANCE] MUST resolve the Registry endpoint through _registry_url, apply a request timeout of the imported REGISTRY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS constant in seconds, and request exactly the path made of the imported REGISTRY_PROJECTS_PATH constant and the imported REGISTRY_ACTIVE_SEGMENT constant, joined by single slashes, relative to that endpoint with no query parameters; decoding still keeps only active ProjectReference values.
judgement.why: The State 7 notes preserve an existing base path, permit only relative supplied paths, join path constants with single slashes, and forbid extra query parameters or host/scheme replacement.

topics.topic: Viewer-entry rate-limiter behavior and concealed refusal response
questions: What rate-limit algorithm, window-boundary rule, key eviction rule and concealed refusal response must the State 7 note state?
What exact rate-limiting algorithm, window boundary, counted attempts, eviction rule and concealed refusal response must `transport_guard` implement?

quotes: _record_viewer_entry_attempt: [BEHAVIOR] MUST drop attempts older than the window from the bucket for the supplied key, return false without recording when the remaining count is at or above the allowed attempts, and otherwise record the attempt and return true. The supplied now and every timestamp it stores are readings of one monotonic clock that cannot move backwards, so the window is a duration measured on that scale and never a wall-clock interval. Each bucket holds at most the allowed attempts, because a refused attempt is not recorded, and it MUST keep total memory bounded by pruning buckets that hold no attempt inside the window, and MUST NOT distinguish its refusal by account state, by whether a capability exists, or by any other fact about the presented credential.

The status of each response a check produces is the status_code of the row of the imported TRANSPORT_GUARD_STATUSES constant selected by the = models.TransportGuardRefusal member named in parentheses.
judgement.why: The State 7 notes define a monotonic sliding window, its boundary and recording behavior, bounded bucket pruning, concealment rule, and the RATE_LIMITED response-status source.

topics.topic: Required test coverage for max_binary_response_bytes and its ordering with the read bound
questions: What must the required test show for application of max_binary_response_bytes itself, rather than only BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES and the start-up ordering between the two bounds?

quotes:
CFG-001: every timeout, TTL, rate limit and bound below exists and is
  applied; its value is the data-provider constant or the start-up setting
  this decision names: the Registry request timeout
  (`REGISTRY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`), the staff and viewer session lifetimes
  (`STAFF_SESSION_TTL_HOURS`, `VIEWER_SESSION_TTL_DAYS`), the viewer-entry
  rate limit (`viewer_entry_rate_limit_attempts` within
  `viewer_entry_rate_limit_window_seconds`), the request body bound
  (`max_request_body_bytes`), the binary response bound
  (`max_binary_response_bytes`) and the binary read bound
  (`BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES`).

CFG-001: one check per bound, each with the bound at its value: a Registry
  request that outlasts the timeout fails as the `timeout` member of
  `RegistryFailureKind`; a staff session and a viewer session are refused
  from the instant their issue time plus their lifetime is reached; the
  viewer-entry attempt after the limit within the window is refused and
  creates no session; a request body over its bound and a binary over its
  read bound are refused before the handler or the response; and the start
  is refused when the read bound exceeds the response bound.
judgement.why: The required test applies the response ceiling by requiring start-up refusal whenever the binary read bound exceeds max_binary_response_bytes, ensuring every readable response is within that ceiling.
